title: Schauberger's wartime diary matches the Kammler sites

tellings.quote: I was able to go and visit the Schauberger family and they opened up their files, the family files.

plain: Viktor Schauberger was an Austrian inventor who worked on unusual flight technology during the Second World War, and his wartime diary is said to line up with the secret sites run by Hans Kammler, the Nazi officer in charge of hidden weapons projects. The British aviation journalist Nick Cook says he went to visit the Schauberger family, who "opened up their files, the family files," and that the diary placed Schauberger at sites such as Jablonec, in what was then Czechoslovakia, between 1942 and 1945. To Cook this ties Schauberger to the Nazis' most secret advanced aircraft research.
